candidate_relations.reason: The reference specifies NPHP13 (nephronophthisis 13) with Caroli disease. Mainzer-Saldino syndrome is a distinct clinical subtype of WDR19-related disease emphasizing retinal and skeletal features. Additionally, C001 adds congenital hypothyroidism as a co-diagnosis not present in the reference benchmark, expanding scope beyond the reference.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Mainzer-Saldino syndrome is a specific WDR19-related ciliopathy subtype (NPHP with retinal dystrophy and skeletal dysplasia), not NPHP13; also adds TG-related hypothyroidism not in reference

candidate_relations.reason: Captures the WDR19-related nephronophthisis component but omits the specific NPHP13 designation and the Caroli disease (intrahepatic bile duct dilatation) which is a required component of the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Correctly identifies NPHP with WDR19 mutations but lacks NPHP13 specificity and Caroli disease component

candidate_relations.reason: Joubert syndrome requires characteristic cerebellar/brainstem malformation (molar tooth sign on MRI). The intracranial MRI here shows no definite structural abnormalities, and the genetic findings point to WDR19-related NPHP13, not Joubert syndrome.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Joubert syndrome is a different ciliopathy with distinct cerebellar/brainstem features (molar tooth sign); no MRI evidence here

candidate_relations.reason: Nephronophthisis alone is a parent category that lacks the required specificity of NPHP13, WDR19 etiology, and the Caroli disease component of the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Generic nephronophthisis label; missing WDR19 specificity, NPHP13 subtype, and Caroli disease

candidate_relations.reason: This candidate is clinically close and includes hepatic ductal dilatation (consistent with Caroli disease) and WDR19 etiology, but does not name NPHP13 specifically nor Caroli disease. It also adds congenital hypothyroidism which is outside the reference benchmark scope.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Captures WDR19 ciliopathy with hepatic ductal dilatation and skeletal features but does not specify NPHP13 or Caroli disease by name; adds hypothyroidism beyond reference scope

candidate_relations.reason: Cranioectodermal dysplasia is a separate clinical entity associated with WDR19 mutations but defined by craniosynostosis and ectodermal anomalies, not matching the NPHP13 + Caroli disease reference. The clinical record does not support this diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Cranioectodermal dysplasia (Sensenbrenner syndrome) is a different WDR19-related phenotype with distinct craniofacial/ectodermal features

candidate_relations.reason: WDR19-related disorder is a parent category that encompasses many phenotypes. It lacks NPHP13 subtype designation and Caroli disease component required by the reference.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Extremely broad label; captures gene but none of the required specificity

candidate_relations.reason: Senior-Loken syndrome requires nephronophthisis combined with retinal dystrophy. The clinical record does not document retinal involvement, and the reference specifies NPHP13 with Caroli disease, not Senior-Loken syndrome.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Senior-Loken syndrome is NPHP with retinal dystrophy; no retinal findings documented here

candidate_relations.reason: WDR19-related disease is a very broad parent label missing NPHP13 specificity and Caroli disease, both required components of the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Even broader than C007; no subtype or Caroli disease component

candidate_relations.reason: Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease is caused by PKHD1 mutations and has a different pathological and imaging profile from WDR19-related NPHP13. The genetic findings here (WDR19 compound heterozygous variants) do not support ARPKD.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: ARPKD is a distinct entity from nephronophthisis; different gene, pathology, and imaging pattern

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis specifies NPHP13 with Caroli disease but does not address the concurrent TG gene variants and hypothyroidism findings documented in the clinical record, suggesting the reference may be intentionally scoped to the primary renal-hepatic diagnosis only.
Caroli disease identification is supported by abdominal MRI showing intrahepatic bile duct dilatation, consistent with the reference.
